title: feat(objectql)!: under `single`, a platform object's organization-less system insert is stamped or refused (C8 stage 8b)
body:
Part of #15212
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

C8 stage 8b, with stage 8c-T-α folded in: its commit `5d1b91e9b` (5 grant rows in 4 test files stamped with the organization their context reads under) is this branch's first commit. Shaped by epic ruling record 6259899486 on #15194: 18.0 is fresh installs, `single` only, and 8b lifts the exemption under `single` only.

## What changes

`Engine.resolveSystemInsertOrganization` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) used to return before it read the posture for every in-reach platform object outside the 9-entry admit list. Those system inserts landed with `organization_id` NULL under every posture.

- **Under `single`** there is no platform-object exemption now. A system insert into a platform object with a tenant column that names no organization goes through the same ADR-0131 D9 decision every application object gets: one organization (the Default Organization) stamps it; zero or several refuse it with `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`. The census puts 35 objects in this newly reached set (44 in reach, minus the 9 admitted).
- **Under a walled posture (`group` / `isolated`)** the #13491 exemption stands, as a named posture condition with a comment citing 6259899486 (item 4). It is not a per-table list.
- **`PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY` does not retire here.** Two readers remain: the walled exemption above, and the engine's diagnostics-only `bypassTenantAudit` isSystem mute (`buildDriverOptions`, every posture). The ledger header now says this. It retires with its walled reader in 18.x (D13). The census tooling and its JSON are unchanged and green, and `lint.yml` is untouched.
- Docblocks are updated in `tenancy/platform-object-tenancy.ts` and `tenancy/system-write-organization.ts`. `packages/core/src/security/system-write-organization.ts` needed no change: its decision function is unchanged, and editing its JSDoc would change published `.d.ts` text for no behavioural reason.

#14570 (`sys_business_unit_member` unadjudicated): under `single` its system-insert row is now stamped (pinned on the real showcase below). Under a wall it still lands NULL, because the exemption stands there in 18.0. So this is **Part of #14570**; the walled half rides 18.x.

## Boot order (the main risk), measured

On a fresh `single` showcase boot (`pnpm dev -- --fresh`, SQLite) the boot is clean and the admin is seeded. Then:
- the admin signs in;
- the admin sends an invitation through `POST /auth/organization/invite-member`, which writes the invitation row and the identity mail;
- the admin creates a record.

A direct DB census after these steps found **0 rows with `organization_id` NULL in every platform table that has the column**, across `sys_setting`, `sys_setting_audit`, `sys_member`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_email`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_user_position`, `sys_audience_binding_suggestion`, `sys_inbox_message`, `sys_notification_receipt`, `sys_webhook`, `sys_business_unit`, the approval family and `sys_record_share`. Every one was stamped with the Default Organization. No producer writes before the Default Organization exists, so no producer needed changing. (`AuthPlugin.start()` creates the Default Organization before the application plugins start, and the seed loader already stamps.)

## Tests

**New pins**
- `packages/objectql/src/tenancy-by-object-classification.test.ts`:
  - under `single`, un-admitted platform objects derive the sole organization;
  - with zero or two organizations they are refused, with the envelope `code`, `status` and `organizationCount`;
  - walled controls (`isolated`, `group`) still land unstamped.
- `packages/objectql/src/system-write-organization.test.ts`: the same split, single against walled, on the #8844 fixture.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-single-platform-insert-default-organization.dogfood.test.ts`, on the real showcase composition:
  - boot, sign-in and an invitation leave no organization-less row in any platform object with a tenant column (with a non-vacuity floor);
  - a bare `isSystem` insert into `sys_business_unit` / `sys_business_unit_member` takes the Default Organization;
  - with a second organization the same insert is refused (`ambiguous-organization`) and nothing is written.

**Tests 8b broke, and how each was fixed.** No pin of a NULL reader was rewritten, and no test was deleted or skipped.
- **Fixtures that hand-registered `sys_organization` / `sys_user` as bare schemas** now declare them as the platform does (`managedBy: 'better-auth'`, so no injected column). Otherwise the first organization's own insert was refused for want of an organization.
  - `runtime/src/system-write-tenancy-autonumber-split.integration.test.ts`
  - `runtime/src/seed-tenancy-autonumber-split.integration.test.ts`
  - `service-messaging/src/notification-organization-follows-event.integration.test.ts`
  - `plugin-approvals/src/status-mirror-cascade.integration.test.ts`
  - `plugin-security/src/sys-audit-log-row-scope.test.ts`
  - `plugin-security/src/granted-by-writer-provenance.test.ts` (plus the Default Organization row a `single` boot holds)
- **PIN fixtures that model organization-less legacy rows** now land those rows through the driver, as the residue an older release left. These are global grants, the retired catalogue bucket, unscoped platform-admin holders and the pre-change ledger. The readers they pin still read NULL rows until 8c (18.x), so each assertion still pins what it pinned.
  - `plugin-security/src/__tests__/legacy-catalog-rows.testkit.ts` and its plugin-auth copy
  - `plugin-security/src/`:
    - `explain-enforce-parity`
    - `explain-removed-member-principal`
    - `explain-principal-person`
    - `explain-asker-gate`
    - `orgless-position-name-fold`
    - `catalog-reference-report`
    - `bootstrap-platform-admin-existing-holder-scan`
    - `controlled-by-parent-chain-middle-master`
    - `sys-audit-log-row-scope` (`LEDGER_BEFORE`)
    - `builtin-positions.boot` (legacy `sys_position` rows)
  - `plugin-auth/src/`:
    - `signup-existing-address-refusal`
    - `sso-register-platform-admin-gate`
    - `driver-fault-auth-log-carriers`
    - `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user`
  - `runtime/src/seed-tenancy-autonumber-split.integration.test.ts` (`[GUARD]` platform residue)
- **One positive control rewritten to the ruled behaviour.** In `plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`, the census control's organization-less `sys_permission_set` insert now reads back with the sole organization under `single`, and unstamped under the wall.
- **Incidental fixtures that only needed an owner** now carry one:
  - `plugin-audit/src/identity-objects-feeds-off.test.ts`;
  - the SCIM rigs `credential-at-rest-posture`, `scim-transaction-scope`, `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user` and `principal-less-producers-system-context`. Their mint carries an organization; the verifier reads the digest alone. The plugin-auth engine pool refuses a database holding an organization row, so adding a Default Organization there was not an option.

- **Dogfood fixtures.** The ablation below proved each of these red only because of 8b.
  - **The Default Organization, asked of the `tenancy` service.** This replaces an empty-`where` `findOne` whose swallowed refusal minted a second organization (the trap that #14570's remainder named):
    - `showcase-scope-depth`
    - `showcase-scope-depth-fallback`
    - `showcase-scope-depth-write`
  - **A grant that carries the fixture organization its sessions are active in:**
    - `activity-withheld-update`
    - `identity-admin-fields-org-peer`
  - **Global grants that an organization-less principal must hold, landed beneath the engine:**
    - `write-door-unreadable-is-not-found`
    - `predicate-write-unreadable-not-matched`
    - `parent-derived-write-refusal-not-visible`
    - `sharing-rule-org-less-caller`
  - **Prechecks that resolved a principal with no organization** now resolve in the organization a `single` session carries. The HTTP doors in the same files use real sessions, and they were green throughout.
    - `wall-package-refusal`
    - `wall-package-doors-refusal`
    - `wall-authoring-trail-doors`
    - `wall-environment-metadata-refusal`
    - `catalog-activation-door`
    - `permission-set-clone-door`
    - `showcase-permission-zoo` (explain is asked in that organization)
  - **Pin rewritten to the ruled behaviour:** `single-tenant-identity-create`. A system `sys_team` insert now takes the Default Organization; the pin used to assert NULL.

The plugin-auth edits are test-only. No plugin-auth source changed. 8b-0f (#24453) had merged into this branch's base before they were made.

## Verification

Everything below is at head `d1838bf96`. Heavy runs went through `os-verify-lock.sh`.

**Build and types**
- **Build:** `pnpm build --concurrency=2` passed 76/76 tasks, after the second `origin/main` merge.
- **Typecheck:** exit 0 in each of objectql, core, runtime, plugin-security, plugin-auth, plugin-audit, service-messaging, plugin-approvals and dogfood.

**Tests**
- **Unit and integration, in the downstream consumers of `@objectstack/objectql`, plus core.** All 48 packages are green after the fixes (vitest per package). Among them:
  - core 2646
  - runtime 7455 (19 skipped)
  - plugin-security 3783
  - plugin-auth 3168
  - rest 6707
  - metadata-protocol 20674
  - service-analytics 4759
  - cli `unit` 4610

  One cli file (`boot-preparation-parity`) timed out at 5 s under parallel load; it passed alone, 37/37. The 18 originally red files re-ran green.
- **objectql:** 446 files, 8369 tests. The only 4 reds were the pins this PR rewrites; those two files now pass 66/66.
- **Dogfood (whole suite, single and walled lanes):** 2291 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run`).
- **Fresh showcase boot:** clean, with the admin seeded and 0 NULL-organization platform rows (see above).

**A1: the walled branch is unchanged**
- The engine's walled branch is the same expression as before.
- The walled controls in both objectql pin files pass, unchanged in shape.
- Every walled dogfood test passes. The ones that broke were rigs whose engine ran at the default `single` and simulated a wall only in plugin services.

**Ablation**
- Tools: `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` and `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`, with a trap restore.
- The mutation restored the exemption in every posture (`!== 'single'` became `!== '8b-ablated'`). Results:
  - **objectql pins:** 5 new cases went red.
  - **dogfood pin:** after a rebuild, with the marker proven present in `dist`, 3/3 went red.
  - **restore:** `git diff HEAD` empty, blob hash matched, rebuild exit 0, marker `--absent` exit 0.
- The same ablation re-ran the 17 other dogfood files that 8b had turned red. All were green with the exemption back, so 8b is their only cause.

**Gates**
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 80 commands, plus a 51-family artifact-roster block. All 128 ran, with exit codes captured before any pipe.
- **Green:** every family not listed below. That includes:
  - `check-platform-object-tenancy-census`, `check-tenant-audit-census` and `check-system-context-census`;
  - `check-adr-0087-registration` (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) and `check-changeset-no-major`;
  - `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:nul-bytes` and `check:type-check-debt`.

  The families that read tests were re-run on the final head.
- **Shallow clone:** `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` and `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` refused on the shallow clone at first. Both are green after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-14`.
- **NOT MEASURED locally:** `check-closing-target-claim`, `check-single-claim-paths` and `check-governed-queue-guard` need PR context that only CI supplies. `check-partof-closing-keyword` was run against this body and is green.

## Acceptance notes

- `mintScimConnectionCredential` (plugin-auth) has no production caller. Under `single` an org-less mint is now stamped with the Default Organization. That is behaviour-neutral, because the verifier never reads the organization.
- A showcase boot logs `[sharing-rule] … expands to NO recipients` for `share_new_inquiries_with_field_ops` with `organization: null` (the rule itself, under regime C). It is not a NULL membership row, and this stage does not touch it.
- Under `single`, a non-system write with no `tenantId` also reaches the decision. The resolver runs for any context without an organization, not only `isSystem`, so such a write into a platform object is now stamped or refused as well. That is consistent with D9 ("every writer").
